findings.rationale: Per-round update stats show the client's uploaded update has norm ratio exactly 0 in rounds 4, 6, 15 and 20, and near zero in rounds 10 and 13 (0.039, 0.058). A zero-norm update is what uploading the global model back without training looks like. In its other rounds the norm is normal (about 1.3-1.6x median). Its local performance is normal (AUC 0.8024, CITL -0.013), so this is not label noise or prevalence shift. No other client's minimum norm ratio goes near zero (the lowest among large clients is about 0.58).

Update norm ratio is exactly 0 in rounds 6 and 10, and near zero in rounds 4, 13, 15 and 20 (0.041, 0.0008, 0.042, 0.006). The client's cos values in those rounds are noise-like (around 0), while its other rounds have normal norms (about 1.1-1.6x median). Its local AUC (0.8219) and CITL (-0.004) are normal, so the fault is in the uploads and not the data. The minimum norm ratio z=-4.0 flag in the summary is consistent with this.

Update norm ratio is exactly 0 in rounds 4, 10, 13 and 20, and near zero in rounds 6 and 15 (0.016, 0.041). In those rounds the cos is noise-like. In its other rounds the norm is normal (about 0.7-1.2x median). Its local AUC (0.8214) and CITL (-0.017) are normal. The zero-norm pattern is the same as OH and MD and is absent from the other 49 clients.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the update, performance, drift, feature and subgroup tools, then checked the update stats for the most suspicious clients. Three clients (OH, MD, SC) show repeated zero-norm updates in roughly 4-6 of 20 rounds, with noise-like cosines in those rounds. That matches a free-rider fault, starting around round 4. Their local performance, calibration and drift look normal, so I attribute the fault to the uploads, not the data. Other weak signals did not hold up: single-subgroup O/E outliers in small groups (MD age 11, SC age 8, AK sex 1, several income groups), a drift flag on MI (z=3.4), and a large update norm for WA (its norm is high but within its size-adjusted expectation, and its cosines decline smoothly). I did not report these as findings. The final narrow subgroup query was too noisy to be conclusive. Budget is fully spent (0.0 remaining). Confidence is moderate because the free-rider call rests on the update-norm pattern alone.
